q: Density is the ratio of _____ to volume of a substance.
e: Density is defined as the ratio of mass to volume of a substance.
Density is a scalar quantity as it only has magnitude and no direction.

q: In the density formula, $\rho$ represents a _____ alphabet.
e: The symbol $\rho$ (rho) used for density is a Greek alphabet letter.

q: In SI unit, density is expressed in _____.
e: In SI units, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$).

q: In CGS unit, density is expressed in gram per cubic centimetre ($\text{g cm}^{-3}$) or _____.
e: In CGS units, density can also be expressed as gram per millilitre ($\text{g mL}^{-1}$).

q: Mass of an object can be measured using a _____.
e: The mass of an object is measured using a balance, while volume is measured using a measuring cylinder.

q: Volume of a substance can be measured using a _____.
e: Volume can be measured using a measuring cylinder.

q: Mass of the object does not change, but the volume depends on the _____.
e: While mass remains constant, the volume of a substance depends on its temperature.

q: If the volume changes, the _____ will change.
e: Since density is mass divided by volume, a change in volume will result in a change in density.

q: According to Table 4.1, the density of water at $4^{\circ}\text{C}$ is _____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: The density of water at $4^{\circ}\text{C}$ is $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ (or $1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$).

q: According to Table 4.1, the density of mercury is _____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: The density of mercury is listed as $13600 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

q: According to Table 4.1, the density of gold is _____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: The density of gold is $19300 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

q: The average density of a human body is a little _____ than water density.
e: The average density of a human body is a little less than water density, which aids in floating.
